verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The formula is the paper's (4.7) with the cumulative mass M = X·A_X(U) substituted for the average. radialFlux (with lam = 0) is X/L · (2ηU − 2Dη A_X(U) − d ∂_η A_X(U)); multiplying through by X and using A_X(U) = M/X with X independent of η turns the numerator into 2ηXU − 2DηM − dM_η, which is literally the form radialFlux_eq_histories states (primitive U = M, primitive (parameterPartial U) = M_η, i.e. differentiation under the integral sign). Two encoding choices: the Lean definition carries a spare exponent increment lam, specialised to 0 at every use I checked (baseFields_beta_flux), and the assembled base field is beta = V_0/X rather than V_0 itself (baseFields_beta_value : xProfile beta p = radialFlux h 0 P.U p / p.1), so vanishing of beta on X > 0 is vanishing of V_0. The '= 0' half is baseFields_beta_exterior, stated in the radius variable R with X = R²/2 and conditional on the two hypotheses U = 0 and M = 0 beyond the radius — which is the paper's 'U = M = J = 0 for X ≥ X_v' — rather than quantified over X ≥ X_v with X_v named. I did not trace that the B at which Exterior is applied in the final assembly is the paper's X_v.
